- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent history shows sustained upward momentum.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >3%, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.
- If forecast peaks sharply and true outcome lags, reduce peak forecast by 5–10% and shift downward slope.
- If forecast consistently underestimates after a strong upward trend, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–2% of recent 7-day average from forecast.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs; if forecast is above 75% of recent 30-day mean, reduce by 3–5%.
- If true outcome is below forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day to avoid persistent overestimation.
- For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day), reduce forecast by 1–2% if true outcome has been below forecast for 5+ days.
